title: HubSpot company event writer: retries, rate-limit handling, and write audit logs
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Internal: Adds HubSpot integration client for writing PLG signal timeline events to Company records with idempotency, retries/backoff, and write audit logs. Feature-flag gated; no customer-facing API changes.
description: Context ENG-2843: We need a reliable write path from the PLG signal pipeline into HubSpot so Sales can act on high-intent triggers. This PR introduces a small HubSpot client + "company event writer" service that can be used by the scoring pipeline to emit HubSpot timeline events (and optionally create tasks later) with sane rate limit handling and auditability. What this PR does: (1) Adds HubSpot client wrapper around the CRM Timeline Events API and Company lookup, using private app auth; (2) Implements retry/backoff with jitter for transient failures (5xx/timeout/429) and respects HubSpot rate limit headers (Retry-After and X-HubSpot-RateLimit-* when present); (3) Adds request batching for timeline event writes to reduce per-event overhead and avoid bursty traffic from scoring backfills; (4) Adds idempotency via a deterministic "write_key" computed from (hubspot_company_id, event_type, event_ts_bucket, external_id) and uses that to avoid duplicate writes across retries/replays; (5) Adds write-audit logs (success + failure) to Postgres for debugging and compliance (who/what/when was written), with redaction of payload fields that could contain PII; (6) Adds a dead-letter queue (DLQ) topic for permanent failures (4xx excluding 429) so we can inspect and reprocess after schema fixes; (7) Adds structured metrics + tracing spans for latency, error rates, and rate-limit throttling. API objects: This PR currently only writes timeline events to Companies. We are NOT creating Deals/Contacts/Tasks in v1 (per PM/RevOps request to keep scope small); those will be handled by HubSpot workflows keyed off the timeline event type once field/property setup is completed (see INT-441). Config: HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN (secret), HUBSPOT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 4000), HUBSPOT_MAX_RETRIES (default 6), HUBSPOT_BATCH_SIZE (default 25), HUBSPOT_RETRY_BASE_MS (default 250), HUBSPOT_DAILY_BUDGET (guardrail to prevent runaway writes), FEATURE_PLG_SIGNAL_HUBSPOT_WRITES (flag, default off). Audit table: hubspot_write_audit(id, write_key, company_id, event_type, attempted_at, status, http_status, hubspot_request_id, error_code, error_message, payload_hash, redacted_payload_json, retry_count, latency_ms). Note: redacted_payload_json removes any user-level identifiers (emails, names) if accidentally included by upstream; only company domain + aggregate signal fields should be present. Testing: Unit tests for retry policy + header parsing + idempotency key generation; integration test harness with recorded responses for 429 and 5xx sequences; migration tests for audit table. Rollout plan: Land behind feature flag; enable for pilot allowlist only (pilot gating is handled in separate PR); monitor hubspot_write_failures and dlq depth; then gradually ramp by segment. Checklist: [x] Unit tests added; [x] Added migrations + rollback; [x] Logging/metrics; [x] Security review notes (no PII; token stored in Vault); [x] Runbook snippets added to /docs/internal/signal-routing/hubspot-writer.md; [ ] Follow-up: add task creation support once HubSpot workflow property set is final (tracked separately).

conversation: Logan Wright (review): "Nice. A couple questions: 1) What do we do when HubSpot returns 429 without Retry-After? 2) Does our retry budget risk hammering them during backfills?" Ethan Park (author): "1) If Retry-After is absent, we fall back to a conservative sleep based on X-HubSpot-RateLimit-Interval-Milliseconds when available, otherwise exponential backoff capped at 30s. 2) Added HUBSPOT_DAILY_BUDGET and batch sizing; plus retries are capped and will DLQ after max attempts. Backfills should be run with the feature flag off until we explicitly enable." David Kim (review): "Please confirm: private app token only, no OAuth refresh flow. Also, timeline event type IDs—are we hardcoding?" Ethan Park: "Yes private app token only. For event type IDs: we are not hardcoding numeric IDs; we write using our internal 'eventType' string and map to HubSpot event template IDs via config. In this PR, the mapping is loaded from env HUBSPOT_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPE_MAP_JSON; default is empty (writer refuses to send if missing) so we don't accidentally write malformed events." David Kim (follow-up): "Can you add a log line when mapping is missing but avoid spamming?" Ethan Park: "Added a one-per-minute rate-limited warning and metric hubspot_event_type_mapping_missing_total." Isabelle Laurent (review): "Idempotency key looks good but I'm worried about timestamp bucketing. If scoring emits the same logical signal twice in the same day we still want suppression; if it emits it a week later we might want a new touch. Can we make the bucket configurable?" Ethan Park: "Good call. Updated write_key to use a configurable bucket duration (default 7d) with env HUBSPOT_DEDUPE_BUCKET_DAYS. This aligns with the cool-down requirements in the PRD." Benji Okafor (review): "Audit log stores redacted payload json—make sure we don't store raw 'notes' fields from upstream. Also add allowlist of payload keys." Ethan Park: "Implemented allowlist: company_domain, signal_type, score, window_days, spend_usd, tokens, concurrency_peak, rate_limit_hits, regions, recommended_offer. Anything else is dropped before hashing/logging." Rafael Mendes (review): "Retries: can we separate connect timeout vs read timeout? We had issues with slow TLS handshakes before." Ethan Park: "Split into connectTimeoutMs=1500 and requestTimeoutMs=4000; both configurable. Also added histogram for hubspot_request_latency_ms."
